text: It is useful to think that our Wi-Fi cards have this concept of time, so for them time is divided into time slots. Okay, so they look at time as divided into time slots. What does this mean? This means that our nodes need to have an internal clock, right? Because you need to measure time into time slots, so you need a clock. And indeed, every Wi-Fi card has got an internal clock. Now, when the nodes are participating in a BSS with access point, they will align their internal clock to the time reference given by the access point. So everyone aligns its own clock to the one of the access point. The access point measures noon, it's noon for everyone, okay. Now, how can the nodes align their own clock on the one of the access point? Through the beacon. So essentially, they will receive the beacon and they will align their clock. Every time they receive a beacon, they pick that as a time reference. The beacon is transmitted by the access point, as we said, more or less periodically every 100 milliseconds. So all the nodes that are part of the BSS.
